name: Taylor University
academic_ranking: Private, non-denominational Christian liberal arts university founded in 1846 in Upland, IN; enrollment ~2,200. Ranked #2 Regional (Midwest) by U.S. News & World Report and #233 national by Forbes. Offers 100+ areas of study / 60+ majors; 99% of students are employed or in graduate school within six months of graduation.
financial_aid: Tuition and fees for 2026-27 are $41,300 (total direct cost ~$53,548 with housing/food/fees). 99% of Taylor students receive financial aid; 600+ scholarships awarded with over $59 million distributed. Merit awards (based on GPA/test scores) range from $11,000 (Director) up to $21,000/yr (President), plus need-based aid via FAFSA (school code 001838): Taylor Fund/endowed grants, Federal Pell/SEOG, Indiana State Grants, Federal Direct Loans, and Work Study. Financial Aid Office: 765-998-5358, finaid@taylor.edu.
facilities_notes: Softball competes on Taylor's Upland, IN campus (approximately 950-acre campus). Specific softball facility/stadium details were not verified from a live official page (athletics site returned bot-protection 403; roster/facility pages not directly accessible 2026-07).
program_reputation: NAIA program competing in the Crossroads League (formerly Mid-Central College Conference). Program underwent a coaching transition, with Grace Glidewell named head coach in June 2025 following interim head coach Doug Gower (58-48 over two seasons) and former head coach Jessica Brown (2023). Taylor athletics has strong recent NAIA success across sports (men's cross country national champions 2020, women's cross country 2022).
